cta.title: Try it on your own words
cta.text: All learning is free, with no ads. It takes a minute to create your first set.

meta.title: How Kolo works — learn words with spaced repetition
meta.description: Pick a language, build sets from your own words and practise a few minutes a day. Kolo brings each word back right before you forget it.

how.title: How Kolo works
how.lead: Kolo is a place for the words you actually need. You add them, practise for a few minutes a day, and Kolo keeps track of when each word should come back.

sections.title: Pick a language
sections.text: Every language you learn is a separate course with its own sets and folders, so Spanish and Norwegian never get mixed up. Kolo supports almost 60 languages and any alphabet or script. You can switch between courses right in the header.

sections.title: Build sets from your own words
sections.text: A set is a list of words on one topic: food, travel, a chapter of a book. Each card has a word and its translation; add an explanation, an example and a part of speech if you like. Sort sets into folders and paste a whole list at once — one word per line.

sections.title: Practise for a few minutes
sections.text: The heart of Kolo is the Perigee session: a few minutes a day, and Kolo decides which words to review and in what format. Flashcards, the quiz and the speed round give you the same words when you want to choose yourself. Five minutes a day is enough to make progress.

sections.title: Kolo brings words back
sections.text: After every answer Perigee, Kolo's review engine, plans the next encounter. Hard words come back tomorrow, familiar ones in a week or a month. The home screen shows how many words are due today, and the Perigee session gets through them in a few minutes.

sections.title: A weekly goal instead of daily pressure
sections.text: Choose how many days a week you want to practise — from 3 to 7. Each day with a session adds a point to the week's orbit; reach your goal and the orbit closes. A missed day burns nothing, and a shield can cover a bad week.

sections.title: Rewards for practice
sections.text: Every session earns XP and raises your level. New levels and closed orbits bring capsules with satellites, ring colours, profile backgrounds and titles. Rewards come only from practice — nothing is for sale.

points.title: Free
points.text: All learning is free, with no ads.

points.title: On any device
points.text: Kolo runs in the browser on your computer and phone. Add it to your home screen and it opens like an app.

points.title: In sync
points.text: With an account, your sets and progress are stored in the cloud and sync between your devices.

points.title: Works offline
points.text: Lost your connection mid-session? Your session is saved and counted as soon as you're back online.

meta.title: Training modes in Kolo — Perigee session, flashcards, quiz and game
meta.description: Perigee session, flashcards, quiz and speed round: four training modes, what each one is best for and how they shape your review schedule.

modes.title: Four training modes
modes.lead: The Perigee session is the main mode: it decides which words to review and in what format. Flashcards, the quiz and the speed round are there when you want to choose yourself. All four teach Perigee what you know.

sections.title: Perigee session
sections.text: One button on the home screen starts a short session across all the sets in your course: up to 20 words, a few minutes. First the words that are due, then a few new ones — no more than 12 a day, so reviews don't pile up. Perigee shows you a new word first, then asks you to spot it among options. Familiar words are checked by how well you know them: with options, typing, a flashcard, by ear or a gap in an example sentence. A mistake comes back a few steps later until it sticks. Inside a set, the Learn button starts the same session with just that set's words.

sections.title: Flashcards
sections.text: See the word, recall the translation, flip the card and rate yourself: “Don't know” brings the word back later in this session, “Forgot” — tomorrow, “Remember” — in a few days, “Know” — the latest. Each button shows when the word will return; on your phone you can swipe: right for “Remember”, left for “Don't know”. A big set goes in rounds of 20 words, and Kolo remembers where you stopped. At the end of a round you see your tough words and can run through them again right away. In the card settings you can flip the direction — recalling the word from its translation is harder and better for speaking — and turn on shuffled order and read-aloud. Best for running through a whole set: a new one, or before a lesson.

sections.title: Quiz
sections.text: A mix of tasks: pick the translation, pick the word, recognise a word from its explanation or type it yourself. The quiz accepts a typo and shows you where it is. You choose which task types to include. A quiz without mistakes earns bonus XP. Best for checking what you really know.

sections.title: Speed round
sections.text: 60 seconds to give as many correct answers as you can, and a streak without mistakes multiplies your score. Quick decisions train instant recognition — exactly what you need in a real conversation.

sections.title: How the modes shape your schedule
sections.text: Every mode tells Perigee how well you know a word — one answer per word per session, the first one. Flashcards use your rating. In the session, the quiz and the game, typing the word exactly counts as “Know”, a correct choice or an answer with a typo as “Remember”, and a mistake as “Forgot”. Reviewing early won't send a word far ahead, and a mistake honestly brings it back.

points.title: Perigee session
points.text: 1 XP for every word, plus 1 more if you got it right the first time.

points.title: Quiz
points.text: 1 XP per question and 1 more per correct answer, plus 10 for a quiz without mistakes.

points.title: Speed round
points.text: 1 XP per correct answer, up to 20 per round.

points.title: Bonuses
points.text: +5 for the first session of the day and +50 for closing the week's orbit. Training XP is capped at 400 a day.

meta.title: Perigee — Kolo's spaced repetition engine
meta.description: How Kolo decides when to bring a word back: the forgetting curve, four rating buttons, growing intervals and the SM-2 algorithm under the hood.

perigee.title: Perigee, Kolo's review engine
perigee.lead: Perigee decides when each word should come back: not too early, so you don't waste time on what you know, and not too late, so you don't forget it.

sections.title: Why “Perigee”
sections.text: In orbit, the perigee is the point where a satellite comes closest to its planet. In Kolo every word moves on its own orbit, and its perigee is the moment it comes back to you — just before it starts to fade.

sections.title: The forgetting curve
sections.text: Without review, memory fades fast: within a few days most new words are gone. Every well-timed review flattens the curve, and the word stays with you longer each time. This is spaced repetition, one of the best-researched ways to learn.

sections.title: Four buttons, four signals
sections.text: After each card you tell Perigee how well you knew the word. Each button shows when the word will return.

points.title: Don't know
points.text: Didn't recall it. The word comes back later in this session and starts over tomorrow.

points.title: Forgot
points.text: You knew it once, but it slipped. It comes back tomorrow, but not from scratch: the next correct answer jumps straight to 6 days.

points.title: Remember
points.text: Recalled it, with effort. A regular step forward.

points.title: Know
points.text: Recalled it instantly. The word goes the furthest.

sections.title: How the gaps grow
sections.text: After the first correct answer a word comes back in 2 days (“Remember”) or 3 (“Know”), after the second in 6 or 8, and from then on the interval is multiplied by the word's ease — and by 1.3 more for “Know”. Ease starts at 2.5: “Know” raises it, “Remember” leaves it as is, “Forgot” and “Don't know” lower it, but never below 1.3. Easy words fly far, and hard ones come back more often.

sections.title: SM-2 under the hood
sections.text: Perigee is built on SM-2, the classic spaced-repetition algorithm behind SuperMemo and many flashcard apps. We simplified and refined it: four clear buttons instead of a six-point scale, each with its own timing, and gentler penalties for mistakes. Every mode updates the schedule, using the first answer to each word in a session.

sections.title: Getting the most out of it

points.title: Rate honestly
points.text: A generous “Know” sends a word away too early. If you hesitated, press “Remember”.

points.title: A little every day
points.text: Five minutes a day works better than an hour once a week.

points.title: Start with the Perigee session
points.text: It begins with the words that are due and adds new ones once those are done.

points.title: New words, a few at a time
points.text: The session adds up to 12 new words a day, so reviews never pile up into a wall.
